article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UNICEF Proposes Four Principles for TB Control in Children in West Papua - ANTARA News Central Papua
article.articleSummary: UNICEF Indonesia proposes four principles for a child-focused TB (tuberculosis) control action plan in West Papua Province, Indonesia, centered in Manokwari. The four principles: 1) select realistic activities with clear, achievable targets; 2) designate responsible parties and deadlines by mutual agreement; 3) outline steps to implement through end-2026 without awaiting new budgets; 4) measure success by child health outcomes rather than budget absorption. Indicators include the number of children screened, treated to cure, and receiving indicated preventive therapy. To optimize implementation, proposed use of existing community health networks—school health programs (UKS), posyandu, puskesmas, village health workers, as well as churches and mosques—and cross-sector coordination with district authorities, schools, village government, religious leaders, and security forces (TNI-Polri). Social protection programs reaching vulnerable families may support TB control in children. Address stigma shaped by experiences of families and patients; stigma contributes to delayed diagnosis and treatment interruption.

article.articleHeadline: Madagascar renforce sa vigilance sanitaire après un deuxième cas d'Ebola au Kenya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Madagascar steps up its health surveillance after a second Ebola case in Kenya.
article.articleSummary: Madagascar has stepped up health surveillance in response to a second Ebola virus disease case reported in Kenya. The Malagasy Ministry of Public Health announced reinforced measures, including enhanced airport health surveillance and readiness of health facilities to detect, notify, isolate, sample, securely transport, and manage suspected cases while preventing infections. Travelers arriving from Kenya will undergo intensified entry-point screening and 21-day health monitoring. Those arriving from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) or who transited through DRC continue to face mandatory 21-day quarantine with health follow-up for entrants. The measures are coordinated with the World Health Organization and technical partners. Madagascar had previously strengthened its system after confirming the first Ebola case in Kenya on Oct 6. This rapid, border-focused response aims to curb potential transmission between Kenya and Madagascar.

article.articleHeadline: 高发期已至！北京疾控发布婴幼儿呼吸道合胞病毒提示
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Peak season has arrived! Beijing CDC issues RSV guidance for infants and young children.
article.articleSummary: Beijing’s Centers for Disease Control and Prevention issued RSV prevention guidance for infants and young children as the autumn–winter peak arrives in 2026. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of infant lower respiratory infections requiring hospitalization, with initial cold-like symptoms that can progress in 2–4 days to cough, wheeze and rapid breathing, potentially leading to recurrent wheeze or asthma. No specific antiviral exists; management is supportive. Preventive measures include avoiding crowded indoor spaces with infants, ensuring ventilation, and strict hand hygiene; avoid exposure to secondhand smoke. China has approved a long-acting preventive monoclonal antibody targeting RSV F protein to block viral entry into lung cells. WHO recommends that infants born during RSV season receive protection at birth; those born before season should start at season onset, with a single dose covering the season. Book through JingTong mini-program or Capital Vaccine Service App.

article.articleHeadline: 高烧后出现红疹？不是普通流感！家长别混淆-新闻中心-北方网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rash after a high fever? It's not the common flu! Parents, don't be confused — News Center — Beifang Net
article.articleSummary: Roseola infantum (infant roseola) is described as a winter illness in China caused by human herpesvirus, typically affecting children aged 6 months to 2 years. Unlike influenza, it begins with a sudden high fever of 39-40°C lasting 3-5 days, during which the child often remains cheerful and active. After the fever breaks, a rose-red maculopapular rash appears, usually non-itchy and non-painful, lasting 1-3 days. Some children may also have cough, vomiting, or diarrhea. Parents are advised to use fever-reducing medicine as directed by a doctor; the rash does not require topical treatment and will resolve without scarring. Warning signs include fever exceeding 5 days, poor overall condition, seizures, or purpuric/vesicular skin lesions—seek urgent medical care. If a child is under 3 months with fever, go to hospital. Source: Beifang Net News Center, published 2026-10-16.

article.articleHeadline: Ministerio de Salud capacita a más de 200 profesionales para optimizar el manejo clínico del dengue frente al riesgo del fenómeno El Niño
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health trains more than 200 professionals to optimize the clinical management of dengue in view of the risk posed by the El Niño phenomenon.
article.articleSummary: Peru's Ministry of Health, via the National School of Public Health (ENSAP), is strengthening dengue management at the primary-care level in anticipation of El Niño–related health risks. In Chiclayo, a six-week, 100-hour course titled 'Dengue Management at the Primary Care Level' trained about 103 professionals—physicians, nurses and obstetricians—from Lambayeque, Amazonas, Cajamarca, La Libertad and San Martín. The program emphasizes early detection, clinical-epidemiological management, triage, surveillance, recognition of warning signs, and referral criteria, aligned with Minsa norms. The training, starting Sept 21, includes virtual and in-person modules, with a final in-person phase in Lima Metropolitana for Diris Lima Centro, Sur, Norte and Este, and yields a 5-credit certification. Viceminister Carlos Espinoza urged vaccination and patient-centered care to prevent dengue deaths. ENSAP continues decentralizing training, having educated over 24,000 health professionals in 2026.

article.articleHeadline: [Why&Next]"러 페스트 의심 사망...고위험 병원체 생물안전 관리 짚어봐야"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: [Why&Next]"Suspected plague-related death... We must examine biosafety management of high-risk pathogens"
article.articleSummary: Death of a researcher at a Russian plague research institute from an unknown pneumonia raises plague infection suspicions. WHO notes no confirmed diagnosis and cannot yet identify the pathogen, so lab exposure cannot be ruled out. Domestic risk to Korea is assessed as very low; surveillance will be intensified for travelers from Russia with fever or respiratory symptoms, and additional quarantines could be enacted if risk rises. If suspected cases occur, they would be transferred to national-designated inpatient beds for isolation and treatment, with antibiotics already secured. WHO reports Russian authorities tested contacts for plague and other pathogens but found no high-risk agents, and no additional severe pneumonia among contacts; two independent investigations reported no lab biosafety incidents. Plague remains endemic in Madagascar, DRC, and Mongolia; pneumonic plague spreads via respiratory droplets and is treatable with antibiotics if diagnosed early. Experts call for strengthened biosafety and clinician readiness.

article.articleHeadline: 해외 감염병 발생하면?..."입국자 검역 강화하고 위험도 따라 단계적 대응"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: If overseas infectious disease outbreaks occur... strengthen entry screening and implement a phased response according to risk.
article.articleSummary: Korea’s Disease Control Agency tightens entry screening and adopts a phased, risk-based response to overseas infectious disease threats. Designation of origin countries as quarantine management regions (QMRs) requires symptomatic reporting via electronic quarantine (Q-CODE) or health status forms for travelers who visit or transit these areas; fever surveillance and interviews assess travel and contact history. If infection is suspected, epidemiologic investigation, specimen collection, isolation, or transfer to national-designated treatment beds follow. As risk rises, areas become “priority quarantine management regions” with mandatory reporting even for asymptomatic entrants. When outbreaks expand, measures extend beyond airport screening to pre/post-entry management, including third-country transit tracking and use of domestic roaming and visa data. Current Russian suspected pneumonic plague case is in early surveillance, with domestic risk deemed low; ongoing WHO information sharing. Examples cited include Africa mpox (2024), Nipah in India and Bangladesh, and Ebola in Uganda and Congo, with Congo DR travelers subject to up to 21 days of active surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Health experts warn of spike in infectious diseases as northeast monsoon arrives in Keralam
article.articleSummary: As of 16 October 2026, health experts warn that the northeast monsoon raises the risk of infectious diseases in Kerala, with intermittent rains elevating vector- and water-borne illnesses. Dengue and leptospirosis are highlighted, alongside waterborne diseases linked to water accumulation. Local bodies are told to strengthen the Arogyabheri epidemic prevention plan, focusing on disease prevention, sanitation, source reduction, disinfection, and spraying; pre-monsoon drives should be conducted. In Ernakulam, influenza cases continue to be reported. Dr. Rajany Jose of Government Medical College Hospital stresses seeking medical care promptly for high fever to avoid complications from leptospirosis and cautions against self-medication. Dr. Sathyajith Nair, secretary of the Indian Academy of Paediatrics, Kochi, calls for proactive measures and sanitation, and notes a high volume of hand, foot and mouth disease, which can resemble chickenpox and also requires medical evaluation. Public should boil drinking water and chlorinate wells, and observe dry days.

article.articleHeadline: Wagub Gorontalo dorong penanganan KLB malaria melalui lintas sektor
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gorontalo Deputy Governor Urges Malaria Outbreak Response Through Intersectoral Collaboration.
article.articleSummary: As of 16 October 2026, a malaria KLB (outbreak) in Gorontalo Province, Indonesia, has reached more than 6,303 cases with 18 deaths, concentrated in Gorontalo City and the districts of Gorontalo Regency, Pohuwato, and Boalemo. Deputy Governor Idah Syahidah Rusli Habibie called for an intersectoral, rapid response to intensify prevention, environmental surveillance, and patient management. The Gorontalo Provincial Government urged strengthened cross-sector and cross-program coordination to halt further deaths. Mining activity was highlighted as a potential driver of transmission in affected areas. The coordination meeting, attended by BPJS Health, the Health Quarantine Agency, and professional health bodies (IDI, PAEI, HAKLI, PPNI) aims to produce concrete measures and assign responsibilities. Gorontalo aims for malaria elimination, or zero cases, by 2030, requiring sustained effort over the next three years.

triage.triage_reason: インドネシア・ゴロンタロ州でマラリアのアウトブレイク（KLB）が宣言され、6,303症例・18死亡という大規模な公衆衛生被害が発生しており、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性）を満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 鉱山活動が感染拡大の一因として指摘されており、環境要因への対応が課題。地方政府はBPJS Health、保健検疫庁、医療専門団体と連携し、2030年のマラリア撲滅を目指す多部門対応を進めている。

article.articleHeadline: Polisi Ramai-ramai Turun ke Kali Baru Bekasi, Bersihkan Eceng Gondok Buat Cegah Banjir dan DBD
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Police officers flock to Bekasi's Kali Baru River, clearing water hyacinth to prevent flooding and dengue fever.
article.articleSummary: Bekasi City police conducted a water hyacinth cleanup along Kali Baru River in front of the Bekasi City Police Headquarters (Jalan Pangeran Jayakarta, Harapan Mulya, Medan Satria) to prevent flooding and dengue fever. Cleaning aims to remove obstructions, restore river flow, and reduce standing water ahead of the rainy season. Police Chief Kombes Putu Kholis Aryana stressed early prevention to protect public safety and health. Based on Bekasi City Health Office data, dengue fever cases reached 2,250 from January to September 2026. The action illustrates Green Policing under the 100-Day Priority Program's 'Safe Public Space' and supports the Indonesia ASRI movement. Authorities urge residents not to dump waste into rivers, maintain drainage, and practice 3M Plus (drain, cover water containers, recycle).

article.articleHeadline: 手足口病活躍程度上升　葉柏強倡學校留意衞生及學童有無病徵
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hand, foot and mouth disease activity on the rise; Ye Pak-keung urges schools to monitor hygiene and whether pupils have symptoms.
article.articleSummary: HFMD activity rising in Hong Kong as of 16 October 2026, per the Department of Health. Professor Ye Pak-keung of HKU's pediatrics notes outbreaks have become more evident this month, centered in kindergartens, nurseries, and primary schools. He attributes this to school reopenings and potentially insufficient preventive measures. HFMD is caused by enteroviruses and affects children year-round, with peaks May–July and October–December. Most cases are mild; incubation 3 days to about a week; early symptoms include fever, sore throat, and oral ulcers. Some viruses, notably enterovirus type 71, are not effectively killed by alcohol sanitizers, hence the emphasis on thorough handwashing with soap and water. Schools should monitor hygiene and pupil symptoms. Original report on RTHK; editor Tam Pui-chen.

triage.headline_ja: 手足口病活躍程度上昇　葉柏強教授、学校に衛生状態及び児童の症状への留意を呼びかけ

article.articleHeadline: В Уганде начали испытывать новую вакцину против опасного штамма Эболы
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Uganda, a new vaccine against a dangerous strain of Ebola has begun testing.
article.articleSummary: Uganda has begun clinical testing of an experimental Ebola vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain (EBOV-BDBV). Trials are under way in Masaka, southern Uganda, with 110 healthy volunteers aged 18–55 to be enrolled by November and followed for one year. In this Phase I study, researchers assess safety and the vaccine’s ability to provoke an immune response for ChAdOx1 BDBV, with efficacy not yet demonstrated. The project is funded by CEPI, and the Serum Institute of India has manufactured and reserved about 620,000 doses for potential use, while roughly 3,000 doses have been shipped to Uganda. Parallel testing is happening in the United Kingdom. If early results are favorable, broader testing would proceed. Bundibugyo virus was first identified in Uganda in 2007 and causes a severe form of Ebola; there is no licensed vaccine for this strain, though vaccines against the Zaire strain exist.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダで危険なエボラ株に対する新たなワクチンの試験が開始

article.articleHeadline: 手足口病活躍程度顯著上升　專家指相信因開學後衞生措施不足所致
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease activity has risen significantly; experts say they believe it is due to inadequate hygiene measures after the start of the school term.
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) activity in Hong Kong has risen sharply, with 9 outbreaks affecting 24 people in the first three days of Oct 11–13. About 90% of cases occurred in kindergartens, preschools, or primary schools. Clinical Professor Ye Pak-keung says the surge follows the school term restart, likely due to crowding and inadequate hygiene; enteroviruses, including EV71, are involved. Alcohol-based sanitizers are not reliably effective; handwashing with soap and water is recommended. Parents are advised to keep children with fever at home and seek prompt medical care for relevant symptoms. HFMD is usually caused by enteroviruses and spread via droplets, nasal secretions, or contact with vesicles on hands, feet, or the mouth. The typical incubation is 3–7 days; initial fever for 1–2 days is followed by blisters on the mouth, hands, and feet; most cases are mild, but rare complications can include myocarditis, meningitis, or encephalitis.

triage.headline_ja: 手足口病の活動が顕著に上昇　専門家は新学期開始後の衛生対策不足が原因と指摘
triage.triage_reason: 香港で手足口病の季節的な増加が報告されているが、重症例や死亡の報告はなく、学校における通常の流行パターンの範囲内であるため、経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 香港（中国特別行政区）での季節性手足口病の増加に関する報告。重症例（心筋炎・髄膜炎・脳炎）はまれな合併症として言及されているが、実際の重症例報告はない。学校を中心とした典型的な流行であり、現時点でフルRRAへの移行は不要と判断。

article.articleHeadline: 146 Warga Tangerang Alami Muntaber, Dokter: Air Jernih Belum Tentu Aman
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 146 Tangerang Residents Suffer From Gastroenteritis, Doctor: Clear Water Is Not Necessarily Safe.
article.articleSummary: On Oct 14, 2026, 146 residents of Serpong Lagoon, Kranggan, Setu, South Tangerang reported vomiting and diarrhea (gastroenteritis). A shared water source from the local water treatment plant is suspected; water samples tested positive for pathogenic Escherichia coli. Pediatric Health Educator Ardi Santoso notes gastroenteritis presents with nausea, repeated vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramps, weakness, and sometimes fever, with onset from hours to days after exposure. The greatest risk is dehydration and electrolyte loss, especially in infants, children, and the elderly; seek medical care for bloody stools, severe abdominal pain, or persistent vomiting with inability to drink. Water can look clear yet be unsafe; possible culprits include pathogenic E. coli, Salmonella, Shigella, norovirus, or parasites. The cluster suggests simultaneous exposure via drinking, cooking, or washing with contaminated water.

triage.headline_ja: タンゲラン住民146人が胃腸炎発症、医師「透明な水が必ずしも安全とは限らない」
triage.triage_reason: 地域限定の水系感染によるE.coli集団胃腸炎事例であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、原因究明と対応状況の続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 原因は水道水の病原性大腸菌汚染と推定され、地域限定の食品・水系感染事例。重症度や死亡者数の情報は記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: 葉柏強：手足口病本月起明顯爆發 幼稚園及小學情況較嚴重 - 香港商報
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Yip Pak-keung: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease Has Clearly Broken Out This Month; Kindergartens and Primary Schools Are More Severely Affected.
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease activity has surged in Hong Kong this October, with kindergartens and primary schools more affected, according to Yip Pak-keung, clinical professor of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at the University of Hong Kong. HFMD typically peaks in May–July and October–December, and the current outbreak began in October, likely due to insufficient preventive measures in schools and children’s weaker physiology. The virus spreads via droplets, nasal secretions, or contact with vesicles on hands, feet, or mouth; incubation is about 3–7 days. Initial high fever lasts 1–2 days, followed by vesicles and ulcers on the mouth, hands, and feet; severe cases may have red rash on the buttocks or genitals. Most infections are mild; a minority develop serious complications such as myocarditis, meningitis, or encephalitis. Alcohol-based sanitizers do not reliably kill enteroviruses; children should wash hands with sanitizer, rest at home if feverish, and seek prompt medical care if symptoms appear.

triage.headline_ja: 葉柏強氏：手足口病が今月から顕著に流行、幼稚園・小学校でより深刻な状況

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tainan's 14th imported dengue fever case: Vietnamese woman who entered Taiwan for work developed symptoms.
article.articleSummary: Taiwan's dengue fever case: Tainan City confirms its 14th imported case, a Vietnamese woman in her 40s from Xiqiao Li, Yongkang District. She first entered Taiwan for work on October 6 and developed a rash, headache, and muscle pain on October 13, later testing PCR-positive at Chi Mei Medical Center, Yongkang. The Tainan Dengue Fever Prevention Center immediately conducted indoor/outdoor fogging around her residence, eliminated breeding sources, and performed vector-density surveys, with plans for further chemical control to reduce transmission risk. Nationally, as of October 15, Taiwan has 201 dengue cases: 14 locally transmitted and 187 imported, with Vietnam the leading country of infection, followed by Indonesia and the Philippines.

article.articleHeadline: Эбола уже охватила 8 провинций Конго: среди детей стремительно растёт число жертв
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has already spread to eight provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo: the death toll among children is rising rapidly.
article.articleSummary: Ebola has spread to eight provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with child deaths rising rapidly. In North Ubangi, two suspected cases have been reported; authorities have not officially confirmed them. North Kivu now accounts for about 25% of confirmed cases among children under 5, with more than half being infants. Doctors Without Borders says in Butembo, from June through September, 30 children were admitted for Ebola treatment, 24 of them dying, most under 5. Experts suspect some infections occurred in hospitals while treating other illnesses, as many families were not sick. Official figures as of October 13 show 9,212 cases and 4,441 deaths. The outbreak continues to spread despite containment efforts.

article.articleHeadline: New Diamine Compounds Show Potent Activity Against Multiple Leishmania
article.articleSummary: 52 second-generation N,N'-disubstituted aliphatic diamines synthesized by reductive amination show potent activity against Leishmania species (L. donovani, L. infantum, L. amazonensis, L. braziliensis), linked to cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis, which WHO reports causes roughly 700,000–1,000,000 new cases annually. The library, developed by Guillermo R. Labadie's team across Argentina, Brazil, the UK, and the US, builds on polyamine metabolism as a drug target; trypanothione-dependent redox defense is absent in mammals, enabling pathogen selectivity. In vitro screening against trypanosomatids (including T. brucei and T. cruzi) revealed 45 of 52 compounds with pIC50 >5 against at least one parasite; several exceeded 6.0. Sixteen compounds outperformed nifurtimox against T. brucei; seventeen against T. cruzi. Against L. donovani, only compound 3i surpassed amphotericin B, though 57% beat pentamidine. The most active compound against T. brucei is 3i (pIC50 7.96; SI 591 vs Vero). Lead SAR shows bulky aryl groups favor shorter linkers; long C10–C12 linkers map to different activity.

triage.headline_ja: 新規ジアミン化合物、複数のリーシュマニア種に対し強力な活性を示す

article.articleHeadline: Russia investigates suspected monkeypox outbreak near Moscow
article.articleSummary: Monkeypox outbreak suspected in the Moscow Region triggered an epidemiological investigation and comprehensive anti-epidemic measures on Oct 15, 2026. Five people who had contact with a suspected carrier were hospitalized for medical observation and diagnostic testing; all are in satisfactory condition with no pronounced symptoms. Authorities have implemented emergency containment including contact tracing, laboratory testing, and widespread disinfection, with in-house advanced diagnostic systems to ensure rapid detection. Testing is ongoing and no new cases have been confirmed. The region had earlier monkeypox cases, including a February 2026 case in Domodedovo; a close contact was hospitalized, and two tourists returning to St. Petersburg from Thailand were later diagnosed. Monkeypox is a viral zoonosis; initial human symptoms include fever, headaches, muscle pains, back pain, and swollen lymph nodes, followed by extensive rashes. Most recover in weeks; some may develop severe illness or die.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Imported malaria case detected in Hue: Female worker with fever for more than a month; tests reveal malaria parasites.
article.articleSummary: Imported malaria case detected in Hue, Vietnam: A female worker born in 1989 from Quảng Trị province, previously treated for malaria in Taiwan (China), was confirmed with Plasmodium falciparum malaria at Hue. She developed fever with chills and sweats for about a month. After returning to Vietnam on 25 September 2026, she sought care and self-medicated, but symptoms persisted. On 7 October 2026, she was admitted to Minh Hóa District General Hospital, Quảng Trị, and transferred the same day to Hue Central Hospital for further assessment. Rapid malaria testing was positive; Giemsa-stained blood smear showed Plasmodium falciparum trophozoites with parasite density ++. The Hue CDC classifies this as an imported malaria case from Taiwan (China); no evidence of local transmission among family or nearby contacts. The patient is being treated per Ministry of Health guidelines. Emphasizes travel history and exposure in fever workups and ongoing surveillance for imported malaria.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has already spread to eight provinces in Congo: among children, the death toll is rising rapidly.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak expanding across eight provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo. As of 13 October 2026, 9,212 confirmed cases and 4,441 deaths reported; transmission ongoing. North Ubangi near the Central African Republic border has two suspected infections not yet officially confirmed. In North Kivu, about 25% of confirmed cases involve children under five, with more than half being infants. Doctors Without Borders reports that in Butembo city from June–September, 30 children were admitted to the Ebola treatment center and 24 died, most under five. Clinicians suspect some pediatric infections occurred in regular hospitals while treating other illnesses, suggesting possible nosocomial transmission, though family members were reportedly not ill. The article highlights continued spread despite medical containment efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Hantaviruses at a Crossroads: Rodent Reservoirs, Spillover Risk, and the
article.articleSummary: Hantaviruses are enveloped, negative-sense RNA viruses maintained in rodent reservoirs worldwide. A Frontiers in Virology review (2026) links rising spillover to environmental change, urbanization, and mobility, noting multi-country clusters and a 2026 expedition cruise-ship event highlighting international preparedness gaps. Old World hantaviruses (Hantaan, Seoul, Puumala, Dobrava-Belgrade) cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Europe/Asia, with case-fatality rates from <1% (Puumala) to ~15% (Dobrava-Belgrade); China bears the largest HFRS burden. New World hantaviruses (Andes, Sin Nombre) cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) in the Americas, with CFRs of 40–50%. Andes virus uniquely demonstrates documented person-to-person transmission within households. Transmission is chiefly via inhalation of aerosolized rodent urine, feces, and saliva; high-risk groups include farmers, forestry workers, military personnel, and laboratory workers.

triage.headline_ja: ハンタウイルス感染症:岐路に立つ、げっ歯類リザーバー、スピルオーバーリスク、ワンヘルスの必要性
triage.triage_reason: 特定の国・地域における急性の発生報告ではなく、ハンタウイルス全般に関する総説記事であり、具体的な公衆衛生上の緊急対応を要する事象は確認されない。
triage.notes: 記事は学術レビュー（Frontiers in Virology, 2026）であり、中国はHFRS疾病負荷が大きい地域として言及されているのみで、具体的な発生事例・アウトブレイクの報告ではない。カナリア諸島・スペインも対象国リスト外であり除外。

article.articleHeadline: Áp xe gan do vi khuẩn
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Liver abscess due to bacteria.
article.articleSummary: In Hanoi, Vietnam, a 58-year-old man, Quang Anh, presented with fever and back pain. Recurrent fever and low back symptoms prompted spine-disease evaluation, but abdominal ultrasound revealed a liver abscess. MRI showed a large, multiloculated abscess in the right liver lobe, about 51×59×79 mm, with a thick wall and surrounding hepatic inflammation, plus a smaller lesion in left-lobe segment IV (~14×12 mm). Ultrasound-guided percutaneous drainage yielded roughly 100 mL of greenish pus, sent for culture and antibiotic susceptibility testing. The organism was Streptococcus intermedius, a member of the oral/GI flora that can cause deep-seated abscesses when mucosal barriers are breached. After antibiotics and drainage, the patient improved, with reduced drainage and pain, and was discharged afebrile. The case underscores that liver abscess can present with nonspecific symptoms and highlights imaging, drainage, and dental hygiene in prevention.

article.articleHeadline: Lào Cai tăng cường các biện pháp phòng, chống dịch tả lợn châu Phi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lao Cai Province steps up measures to prevent and control African swine fever
article.articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) continued to affect Lao Cai Province, Vietnam, through Oct 12, 2026, with 2,844 pigs culled from 418 households across 128 hamlets in 36 communes, totaling over 127,377 kg. Although 22 of 36 communes had no new cases after 21 days, October outbreaks persisted: 67 households across 19 hamlets in 5 communes were affected and 426 pigs were culled (23,507.5 kg). ASF is highly contagious among pigs and wild boar; it does not infect humans. The province intensified surveillance, field guidance, and vaccination deployment per plan, along with disinfection and sanitation. Authorities supplied 3,750 liters of disinfectant and collected 26 samples for testing. Transport and slaughter controls on roads and border routes were strengthened to curb spread, reinforced by a strict “five no’s” rule for farmers to improve early detection and containment.

article.articleHeadline: Taiwan monitors rumours of pneumonic plague outbreak allegedly spreading from Russia to China
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague rumors prompt Taiwan to monitor potential outbreak originating in Russia and spreading to China. Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai says health authorities may tighten border quarantines after briefing two weeks earlier and ongoing monitoring of online reports. The government has contacted the WHO to verify whether an Irkutsk laboratory worker’s death from pneumonia was due to pneumonic plague; no pathogen tests have returned positive results, so plague cannot be confirmed. Between Oct 1–2, the worker died at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute; Russian investigations found no lab accident; cause listed as pneumonia of unknown origin. About 200 contacts are under observation; no plague infections confirmed. WHO says risk to the general population appears low; seeks information from Russian authorities. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis; pneumonic form affects the lungs and requires rapid treatment; Taiwan has border measures in place and stands ready to enhance them if needed.

triage.headline_ja: 台湾、ロシアから中国へ拡大しているとされる肺ペスト流行の噂を監視
triage.triage_reason: 肺ペストのアウトブレイクに関する未確認の噂であるが、台湾政府が国境検疫強化を検討しWHOに照会するなど政府・社会的関心が高まっており、異常性と越境拡大の懸念からフルリスク評価への移行が妥当。
triage.notes: ロシア・イルクーツクでの研究所職員の死亡原因は『原因不明の肺炎』とされ、病原体検査はいずれも陽性反応なし。中国への『拡大』は噂の段階であり確認された感染例はないため、対象国リストにおける実際の発生国として確定できない。WHOはリスクを低いと評価しているが、台湾当局は監視と国境措置強化を検討中であり、続報の推移を要確認。

article.articleHeadline: Kronologi Muntaber Serang 145 Warga Serpong Lagoon Tangsel, Diawali Aduan Air Keruh
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Timeline of a gastroenteritis outbreak that struck 145 residents of Serpong Lagoon, South Tangerang, starting with reports of murky water.
article.articleSummary: Escherichia coli–associated gastroenteritis outbreak hits 145 residents of Serpong Lagoon, Keranggan, Setu, South Tangerang, Banten, Indonesia. As of 16 October 2026, infections rose after murky water was reported in mid-September 2026. Water samples included two from bottled water at homes (Block A, B1) and one from a water tower/IPA run by PT APS. On 7 October at 20:00, health workers noted initial cases with fever, diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting, increasing to 27 by 8 October. Dinkes Tangsel and Puskesmas Keranggan launched epidemiological investigations on 9 October, conducting interviews and digital surveys; by 10 October, 137 cases were recorded and 58 were referred to facilities, with some children hospitalized at Eka Hospital. Lab confirmation identifies E. coli as the cause; the water supply is implicated as the ongoing transmission source.

triage.headline_ja: 混濁した水に関する苦情から始まった、南タンゲラン・セルポンラグーン住民145人を襲った胃腸炎（ムンタベル）発生の経緯
triage.triage_reason: 単一地区での水系感染による集団胃腸炎（E. coli）であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限の懸念は低いが、継続的な汚染源（給水設備）の存在と入院例があるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 単一集合住宅地区（Serpong Lagoon）内での局所的な水道汚染によるアウトブレイクで、地元保健当局が調査・対応中。地域限定的で国際的波及リスクは低いが、汚染源（PT APS管理の給水塔）が未解決であれば感染拡大の可能性あり、続報を要する。

article.articleHeadline: Peppermint Oil Microemulsion Shows Potent Larvicidal Power Against Aedes
article.articleSummary: Peppermint essential oil microemulsion PME-05 developed by Brazil's FUNED acts as a water-compatible larvicide against Aedes aegypti, potentially aiding dengue, Zika, chikungunya control. The oil profile is menthol 50.17%, menthone 23.02%, pulegone 4.21%, D-limonene 3.28%, eucalyptol 2.42% across ~100% of oil. In lab tests on third-instar larvae in dechlorinated water, LC50 was 175.7 µg/mL and complete mortality occurred at ≥250 µg/mL after 24 h. PME-05 uses 5% peppermint oil with a surfactant/co-surfactant/water mix, producing stable nanoscale droplets and addressing hydrophobic/volatile limits. Observed effects include reduced mobility, paralysis, darkening, and death; some larvae remained briefly viable after locomotion ceased. This supports essential oils as renewable, multi-target insecticides for dengue, Zika, and chikungunya vector control.

triage.headline_ja: ペパーミントオイルマイクロエマルションがネッタイシマカに対し強力な幼虫駆除効果を示す
